paras: The attempted lynching of Gust Johnson took place near Phillips, Wisconsin, on July 12, 1888, when a crowd of railroad section hands and citizens put a rope around the neck of Johnson, a homesteader accused of chaining and flogging his young son. Johnson was released alive after promising never to whip the boy again, but only after the crowd flogged him and ducked him in a railway water tank. Newspapers that carried the story treated the crowd's action as deserved punishment of a "cruel and unnatural father."

Johnson lived in the township of Worcester in Price County, near Phillips. According to a Phillips dispatch of July 15, he had for some time punished his 10-year-old son harshly, and on Sunday morning, July 8, tied the boy to a post with a log chain and flogged him. An Ashland dispatch instead said the boy was chained to a "chair." The boy escaped on Monday night and wandered in the woods without food until Wednesday, when a Wisconsin Central railroad crew found him nearly starved.

After hearing the boy's story, the railroad men went with other citizens to Johnson's house on Thursday night. The Ashland correspondent of the St. Paul Globe wrote that they put a rope around his neck and dragged him to a tree, while the Phillips dispatch said they strung him up to a limb and lowered him when he "begged so hard and pitifully." Johnson promised never to whip the boy again and was let go.

The crowd did not end there, however. Two later dispatches said Johnson was "soundly flogged" or given "a sound threshing" before being taken to the railway tank, where, in the Globe's words, he received "a ducking that nearly drowned him."

The boy was taken in charge by citizens of the settlement. Reports that surfaced afterward claimed Johnson had kept his son chained for weeks at a time on bread and water. No report of an arrest of either Johnson or members of the crowd appears in the coverage.

The St. Paul Globe ran the first account on July 14 under the headline "On Promising to Reform He Escapes With a Ducking," calling the outcome "a just punishment." A Phillips dispatch printed in the McCook Tribune in Nebraska was headlined "A Brutal Father Fittingly Punished" and praised "rightly indignant citizens," while the Owosso Times in Michigan headed its Ashland version "Horrible Cruelty to a Boy." Later in July, Wisconsin state-news columns in the River Falls Journal and the Kenosha Telegraph reprinted the Globe's story as "A Cruel Father: His Narrow Escape from Lynching by Indignant Railroad Men." None of the reports mentioned race, and all of them presented the boy's account and the crowd's punishment without question.

The Globe's account mentions only the rope and the ducking, while the Ashland July 14 and Phillips July 15 dispatches add that Johnson was also flogged; the Phillips report, the most local and detailed, also says he was actually strung up before being lowered.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of Gust Johnson
bases: A crowd of railroad men and citizens put a rope around Johnson's neck and took him to a tree in what the papers called an intended lynching, then flogged and ducked him instead of killing him (A1, A2, A3).

A crowd of section hands and citizens acting without authority to punish Johnson for alleged cruelty to his son threatened to hang him, but he was released alive after a flogging and ducking (A1, A2, A3); no one was killed, so it does not meet the definition.
Separate dispatches from Ashland (July 13 and July 14) and from Phillips (July 15) agree on the rope, the tree, the release on a promise and the ducking at the tank (A1, A2, A3).

accounts.label: Ashland special to the St. Paul Globe (July 13)
accounts.gist: The section hands put a rope around Johnson's neck and dragged him to a tree; on his promise he was released after a ducking at a water tank. No flogging of Johnson is mentioned.

accounts.label: Ashland dispatch (July 14)
accounts.gist: Railroaders and citizens were going to lynch Johnson but released him on his promise; he was 'again taken in hand', soundly flogged and ducked in the railway tank.

accounts.label: Phillips dispatch (July 15)
accounts.gist: On Thursday night the crew and other citizens strung Johnson up to a tree limb, lowered him when he begged, gave him a sound threshing and marched him to the railway tank for a cold bath.

framing.detail: The Globe headlined 'On Promising to Reform He Escapes With a Ducking' and called the outcome 'a just punishment administered to a cruel and unnatural father'.
The McCook Tribune headlined 'A Brutal Father Fittingly Punished' and described 'summary punishment by rightly indignant citizens'.
The Owosso Times headlined the story 'Horrible Cruelty to a Boy', centering the father's alleged acts.
Wisconsin state-news columns ran it as 'A Cruel Father: His Narrow Escape from Lynching by Indignant Railroad Men', calling Johnson 'the brute'.
